description: Re, solar god of Egypt: he creates the world, crosses the sky every day, fights chaos at night, and punishes men with his Eye.

hero.hook: Every dawn is a victory. Without Ra's boat, the world would fall back into nothingness.

blocks.text: **D** (or Râ) is not just the sun. For the Egyptians of **Heliopolis**, city of solar worship near present-day Cairo, it is the very principle of existence: creating the world, then defending it every night against nothingness.

For three millennia, his figure crossed the state religion. Understanding Re means understanding how Egypt thought about the birth of the universe, the fragility of order, and why each dawn is a victory to be reconquered.

Before time, there is the **Noun**: dark, infinite water, full of germs. The  describes the appearance of **Atum**, “the completed one”. It generates itself and emerges on the **Pierre Benben**, first solid point. [[The Heliopolitan cosmogony]]

blocks.caption: Atum emerges from the Noun on the Benben Stone.

blocks.text: In Heliopolis, the priests maintained a sacred bird, the **Bénou** (ancestor of the phoenix), supposed to be the soul of Re and to land on the Benben to announce a new cycle.

Alone, Atoum creates **Cabbage** (air) and **Tefnut** (humidity), then **Geb** (Earth) and **Nut** (Sky), separated to leave a living space. **Osiris**, **Isis**, **Seth** and **Nephthys** are born: with Atum, the **great Ennead** (the nine). The  would later merge Atum and Ra into a single creative figure. [[Egyptian divine syncretism]]

sections.title: The emergence of the world: the primordial tumulus

blocks.text: During the day, Re sails on the boat **Mandjet**. At dusk, he passes over the **Mesektet** and crosses the twelve hours of the , the world of the dead. This is not a rest: it is a war against **Isfet**, disorder. [[Douat]]

blocks.caption: The solar boat of Re, daily engine of time.

blocks.text: From the 4th Dynasty onwards, almost all the pharaohs had “Re” in their name: they called themselves “sons of Re”, guarantors of the solar cycle.

The serpent **Apopis** seeks to overturn the boat or to drink the waters of the celestial Nile. **Seth** himself sometimes defends the bow. When Re is reborn at dawn in the guise of **Khépri**, the scarab, it is **Maât** (balance) which wins once again. An eclipse? Apopis almost won.

sections.title: The Maat against the Isfet: the perilous journey of the boat

blocks.text: Even Ra is getting old. In the story of "The Destruction of Men", his bones become silver and humanity conspires against him. Offended, he unleashes his fiery Eye: the goddess , bloodthirsty lioness. [[Sekhmet]]

blocks.caption: Sekhmet, the Eye of Re, before becoming Hathor again.

blocks.text: The massacre threatens to extinguish creation. Rê brews thousands of jars of beer tinted with red ocher, poured onto the fields. Sekhmet, believing she is drinking blood, becomes drunk and calms down: she becomes the sweet **Hathor**. The myth explains evil, and justifies the feast of drunkenness, where people drank to celebrate the salvation of men.

sections.title: The revolt of men and the destructive eye

blocks.text: In the New Kingdom, the Theban god **Amon** merged with Re: **Amon-Rê** was born, “King of the Gods”, invisible creator and visible sun. For him the largest sanctuaries rise, like the . [[Karnak Temple]]

Pyramids and obelisks petrify the sun's rays to raise the pharaoh towards his heavenly father. Even the reform of **Akhenaten**, which imposed the cult of **Aten** (the disk), radicalized an already solar idea. Ra remains the insurmountable symbol of Egyptian stability.

**D** creates the world from Heliopolis, defends it every night in his boat against **Apopis**, and punishes then saves humanity through the Eye **Sekhmet**. Becoming **Amon-Rê**, he reigns at the top of the Egypt of the pharaohs.

sections.title: Posterity and fusion: the avatar Amon-Re
